title: The Longest Continuous Human Presence
attribution: Adapted (trimmed) from the Wikipedia article "International Space Station," available under CC BY-SA 4.0.
body: The International Space Station (ISS) is a space station in low Earth orbit. It is operated by five partner space agencies: NASA (United States), Roscosmos (Russia), ESA (Europe), JAXA (Japan), and CSA (Canada). It is the first space station built, maintained and crewed through international cooperation and the largest human spacecraft ever constructed. Since 2 November 2000, it has hosted the longest continuous human presence in space.

The station orbits between 51.64 degrees north and south, at about 400 kilometres (250 miles) above Earth, below the Van Allen radiation belts and most space debris. Its orbit takes it at 7.67 km/s (27,600 km/h; 17,200 mph) roughly every 93 minutes around Earth, 15.5 times a day. Measuring 109 m (358 ft) with solar arrays by 73 m (239 ft), it is as large as a full-sized football field.

The station is a modular space station divided into two main sections: the Russian Orbital Segment, developed by Roscosmos, and the US Orbital Segment, built by NASA, ESA, JAXA, and CSA. In total, the station consists of 43 different modules and elements. The first ISS module was launched in 1998, and long-term occupancy began with the arrival of the Expedition 1 crew on 2 November 2000.

Based on the passage, why does the ISS orbit "below the Van Allen radiation belts and most space debris"?
options: To reduce astronauts' exposure to harmful radiation and lower the risk of collisions with debris
To make the station more visible from Earth at night
To allow it to communicate directly with the Moon
To keep its solar panels charged at all times

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why is the ISS considered "the first space station built, maintained and crewed through international cooperation"?
options: It required continuous cooperation among five separate national space agencies rather than being run by a single nation
It was the very first object ever placed into orbit around Earth
It was built entirely without any government funding
It was designed to operate without any human crew at all

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the overall point of the passage?
options: The ISS is a large, internationally operated space station that has maintained a continuous human presence in orbit since 2000
The ISS is a small research satellite with no crew aboard
The ISS was built and is operated entirely by a single country
The ISS has been unoccupied since it was first launched

questions.prompt: As used in the passage, what does it mean that the ISS is a "modular" space station?
options: It is built from separate, connectable sections rather than as a single unbroken structure
It can only be assembled and disassembled on Earth
It changes its orbit every few months
It is powered entirely by a single large engine

options: To show that separately built national segments were integrated into one continuously operated international station
To argue that the two segments operate completely independently of each other
To suggest that the segments were built by competing rather than cooperating nations
To prove that only two countries were involved in building the ISS

options: It is a large, modular station built from dozens of connected sections contributed by different space agencies
It is a single, uninterrupted structure launched all at once in 1998
It has no internal divisions or separate modules of any kind

options: Unbroken and uninterrupted since it began
Limited to a single astronaut at a time
